messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the canary bump to v2 in eu-west, the routing dashboard lit up with a surge of compatibility warnings and a bunch of automatic fallbacks to v1. Spike started ~08:23 and persisted. @noah any idea if this ties to the header/quota change? :warning:

noah: Yep, I see the same. Tracing suggests requests missing the `x-client-version` header are being classified as unknown -> routed to v1. We pushed a stricter header enforcement in the quota service yesterday. :eyes:

maria: That matches what I'm seeing. Canary was 30% -> 60% this morning (deploy-bot reported). Some customers are getting degraded latencies because v1 pools are saturated.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout event: service=inference-api, env=eu-west, v2_percent=30->60, user=release-cd.

liz: We should avoid breaking clients without a soft grace. Proposal: if header missing, emit metric `client.version.missing` and only route to v1 when `client.version.missing_rate > 5%` for 5m window. Until then, route by best-effort affinity. Also add a dashboard panel for that metric.

samir: 👍 agree. Also, console UX: show a small non-blocking banner for orgs with traffic hitting the fallback policy, with copy + instructions to upgrade SDKs. We can include a link to a self-serve header shim for older clients.

noah: Quick config snippet from quota-service that caused this (current):
```
# quota routing rule (pseudo)
if not headers['x-client-version']:
  classification = 'unknown'
else:
  classification = parse_version(headers['x-client-version'])
```
We tightened unknown -> failover routing yesterday to reduce v2 noise. Should relax to `unknown -> best-effort` for now.

maria: Can we do a fast rollback to relaxed behavior + sampling? I want to avoid a full config rollback if possible.

ray: I can add an alert and create a runbook. Steps I propose:
1) Update quota-service rule to: `unknown -> best-effort` with tagging metric `client.version.missing_sampled` at 10% sample.
2) Deploy change to staging, run synthetic probe against the routing path.
3) If fallbacks drop and v2 latency stabilizes, roll forward to prod canary patch.
4) Create dashboard panel highlighting `client.version.missing` and `fallback.rate` by org.

jess: I'll own the console banner copy + link to the shim doc. Draft: “We detected older SDKs in your traffic. For best performance, upgrade to the latest SDK or enable the temporary header-shim in the Console.” Will post copy in #devex for review.

maria: Great. Who's taking the runtime change? @noah or @ray?

noah: I can push the relaxed rule and sampling toggle. Will open a small PR and tag for expedited review.

ray: I'll provision the dashboard panels and add the alert rule: `fallback.rate > 3% for 5m` to page on-call. Also will add a non-pager low-priority alert for `client.version.missing > 1%` to track regressions.

liz: Should we also add a telemetry tag for rollout-stage so we can filter 30/60/100 easily in the graph?

maria: Yes — add `rollout_stage` label to all metrics emitted during a rollout. We need that to correlate with canary percent.

noah: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/482 (draft) — contains relaxed rule + sampling flag. Will merge after one quick QA.

samir: Console banner PR incoming from me in ~30m. I'll include the shim toggle link and a short FAQ snippet.

maria: Thanks all. Action items: noah -> deploy relax & sampling; ray -> dashboards + alerts + runbook; jess/samir -> banner + doc; liz -> add rollout_stage label to metrics. We'll meet in 20m in #eng-standup if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Action required: expedited release approvals needed for PRs linked to canary rollback mitigation.

ray: Logged runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/v2-fallback-mitigation (draft). Will update after the patch lands.

maria: Monitoring update: after noah's patch we should watch `v2.latency.p50`, `fallback.rate`, and `client.version.missing_sampled` for the next hour. If fallback.rate remains >5% we escalate.

noah: Patch merged and deployed to canary at 08:40. Rolling to 20% first.

maria: Seeing immediate drop in fallback rate in the sampling panel. Nice. Will keep an eye. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. :heart:
